title: The Halting Problem: Why Some Questions Can Never Be Answered by Computation
question: Can a computer program ever determine, in general, whether another program will finish running or loop forever?
summary: In 1936, Alan Turing proved that no algorithm can exist that decides, for every possible program and input, whether the program halts. This is not a matter of insufficient cleverness or computing power; it is a hard limit built into the nature of computation itself, with consequences reaching into mathematics, software engineering, and the philosophy of mind.
